## Summary

Vinit designs the layer other engineers build on top of. His work centres on
distributed communication infrastructure: systems that dispatch millions of
messages a day across many third-party providers while guaranteeing each one is
processed exactly once, retried only when it is safe to, and paced so no vendor
rate limit is breached.

## What he is known for

1. Abstraction design — a plug-and-play communication framework putting 8+
   telecom/messaging provider integrations behind a single static interface.
   Each integration runs its own vendor-specific methods but returns a defined
   Pydantic model, normalised into one standard format the rest of the
   application understands (for example, a vendor's `call_completed` becomes a
   canonical `ANSWERED`). Adding a provider requires no change to routing.
2. Reliability — distributed debounce using Redis pipelines and atomic TTL
   operations to collapse message bursts into a single processed event across
   multiple server instances with no sticky sessions; a strict error taxonomy
   separating terminal vendor failures from retryable system failures;
   exponential backoff giving at-least-once delivery.
3. Efficiency at scale — roughly 80% of per-job context reads served from Redis
   instead of PostgreSQL; query hardening that cut 40+ seconds from report
   execution; N+1 elimination; ~20% cloud cost reduction in an earlier role.
4. Zero-to-one ownership — bootstrapped nine services end to end (Docker,
   dependency management, async DB pooling, CI/CD, deployment) and continues to
   operate them in production.
5. Refactoring discipline — 36% of his commits in the core service were pure
   refactoring, paying down technical debt he created himself.

## Scale

- 10M+ API calls / interactions per day through systems he designed
- 9 services owned across ingress, core orchestration, egress and agent runtime
- 8+ provider integrations behind one interface
- ~139k lines across 713 commits in 14 months
